name: Canara Bank
title: Canara Bank - 532483 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Canara Bank Q1 FY27 beat its own guidance on most metrics (credit cost 0.49%, GNPA 1.57%, NIM 2.52%), but net profit grew only 2.19% on a treasury drop and ECL provisions of about ₹10,000-12,000 crore loom.

summary.headline: Canara Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 2.19% YoY to ₹4,856 crore, with NII crossing ₹10,000 crore and CET1 at 12.91%.
summary.overview: Management reported global business up 14.37% YoY to ₹29.05 lakh crore, with advances up 17.97% and deposits up 11.63%. NII rose 13.39% YoY to ₹10,215 crore, the first time above ₹10,000 crore. Asset quality improved: gross NPA 1.57% (down 112 bps YoY), net NPA 0.36%, PCR 94.76%, and credit cost 0.49%. Profit was supported by ₹1,947 crore of other income, largely PSLC sale gains, against ₹654 crore from investment sales, while treasury gains fell sharply YoY. Management flagged an incremental ECL provisioning requirement of about ₹10,000-12,000 crore, to be absorbed over two years.

financial_highlights.metric: Other income (per analyst's figure, Q1 vs Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.change: vs ₹393 crore in Q4 FY26; Q1 FY26 was ₹1,684 crore PSLC income

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances ₹7,64,675 crore, up 21.20% YoY. Retail RAM ₹3,19,893 crore, up 35.88%, with housing ₹1,29,036 crore (+17.85%) and vehicle ₹27,315 crore (+26.34%).

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances ₹1,68,815 crore, up 15.12% YoY. MSME and agri carried most of Q1 slippages (₹697 crore and ₹727 crore respectively).

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loan book ₹2.59 lakh crore: agri gold ₹1.51 lakh crore and retail gold ₹1.07 lakh crore. LTV around 60-65%.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and associates
segments.commentary: Around 5 subsidiaries and 5 associates; Canara HSBC Life and Canara Robeco listed last year. Management said they contributed about ₹320 crore of profit to the parent this year.

guidance_outlook: NIM guidance of 2.50-2.60% retained; management said it could exceed 2.60% but kept the range given headwinds.
Credit cost expected to rise by about 4-5 bps on a run-rate basis after ECL transition, per management (initially said up to 10 bps).
ECL: incremental provision of about ₹10,000-12,000 crore (about 1.2-1.25% of RWA), to be absorbed over 2 years versus the 5-year RBI window; dry run by October.
FCNRB: guidance of USD 2.3-2.5 billion; USD 775 million raised in July so far, with a target above USD 1 billion for the month.

ROA guidance of 1.01-1.05%; management said 1.01-1.02% would be acceptable. Deposit growth guidance of 9-10%, with management aiming for 11-12%. Plans to open 250 branches this year (34 opened so far).
Credit pipeline of about ₹50,000 crore: 45 accounts sanctioned but undisbursed (about ₹18,000 crore) and 47 accounts (about ₹32,000 crore) in hand.
capex_capacity: Branch network 10,131; plan to open 250 new branches in FY27, 34 opened so far.
Digital spend earmarked above ₹3,000 crore, about 8% of total IT cost, with a substantial share toward AI.
Credit pipeline of about ₹50,000 crore across 92-100 accounts.
demand_pricing: Advances growth was helped by ECLGS 5.0: about ₹18,000 crore eligible, ₹11,000 crore-plus sanctioned and ₹10,000 crore-plus disbursed, with ₹5,000-6,000 crore still to come. Management said the spill-over could support growth in coming quarters.
Corporate pricing has improved by about 10-20 bps in some cases; management said incremental lending is being done above the average yield.
Yield on advances was 8% against 6.90% on investments. Yield on advances fell 29 bps QoQ, while cost of deposits fell 27 bps.
Bulk deposit cost was 6.58% last month and is falling about 20-30 bps a month. FCNRB is being raised at about 6.50%.
CASA ratio is 29.70%; SA individual deposits up 12.48% and retail term deposits up 9.10%. CD ratio rose from 75% to 80%.
Corporate book: 86% rated A and above. RAM yield is about 50 bps above corporate yield, per management.
Fee income: YoY growth of 5.35%; YTD fee income is down less than ₹200 crore versus Q4, because some commissions were booked in Q4.
Q1 slippage ₹1,781 crore: agri ₹727 crore, MSME ₹697 crore, retail ₹326 crore, gold ₹20-30 crore. Total SMA is below 3%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SMA-2 rise from ₹1,394 crore to ₹3,482 crore, and what is the ECLGS 5.0 assessment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to 2-3 government-guaranteed consortium accounts that oscillate between SMA-0, 1 and 2; one account moved to SMA-2 and has since returned to SMA-0. Total SMA is below 3%. ECLGS 5.0: ₹18,000 crore eligible, ₹11,000 crore-plus sanctioned, ₹10,000 crore-plus disbursed.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the other income jump (PSLC, treasury), and what drove provisions of ₹3,780 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury gains fell YoY (Q1 FY26 ₹1,617 crore, Q1 FY27 ₹654 crore from investment sales) because arbitrage was absent and yields had hardened. PSLC income is concentrated in Q1 and part of Q2 (₹1,947 crore in Q1). Provisions rose on income tax, and ₹300 crore was provided for PLI staff incentives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact and how will it be absorbed?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental provisioning of ₹10,000-12,000 crore including about ₹2,000 crore for M2M on investments. CET1 would fall by about 1.2-1.25%, against a regulatory minimum of 8% CET1. Provision to be absorbed over 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path for NIM and CASA, and the blended cost of bulk deposits?
qa_highlights.answer: Bulk deposit cost was 6.58% last month and is falling about 20-30 bps per month. Management is replacing bulk deposits with retail deposits and FCNRB, and says NIM will stay in the 2.50-2.60% range for now.

qa_highlights.question: Are yields stabilising, and how is incremental lending priced?
qa_highlights.answer: RAM share rose from 58% to 59%. Sub-7% legacy loans are being reset higher at repricing; corporate pricing is up 10-20 bps in some deals. Management said yields have largely stabilised, but this depends on MPC decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost impact of ECL and the monsoon risk to the agri book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a run-rate increase of about 4-5 bps after ECL. The agri book is not large, and distress-district dispensations from SLBC/DLTC and Fasal Bima would help manage any stress.

risks_watch: ECL transition: incremental provisioning of ₹10,000-12,000 crore, plus possible M2M losses on the investment book, which management could not quantify precisely.
Treasury and PSLC gains are one-time in nature and fell sharply in treasury YoY, so the profit mix may not repeat in coming quarters.
Profit growth of 2.19% YoY trails advances growth of 17.97%, and NII growth of 13.39% also trails advances growth.
Repo-linked assets (53% of portfolio) and possible deposit-rate competition could keep pressure on NIM.
SMA-2 movement and the agri/MSME stress: monsoon risk to the KCC book, and continued consortium account oscillation.
Fee income YTD is down less than ₹200 crore versus Q4; the YoY growth is 5.35%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on headline growth, asset quality and capital, with management saying every guidance metric was beaten. Noticeably more cautious on NIM, the ECL impact, and sustainability of PSLC and treasury gains; several answers relied on qualitative reassurance rather than hard figures.
key_quotes: So whatever the performance we have given, we have bettered everywhere on count of guidance whatever we have given.
Even if we are not raising any capital, we will be very peacefully selling through new norms of ECL.
Repricing is also, I mean, I think it is plateau. It is all done.
So, I guess, there will be not much effect. And KCC portfolio also not very huge at our bank, you see.
Yes, our dependency on bulk deposit is more considering our CASA percentage is less than 30%, around 29.70%.

adds.what: 250 new branches in FY27 (34 opened so far; network 10,131)

growth.why: Management guides deposit growth of 9-10% (aiming 11-12%), NIM 2.50-2.60%, and 250 branch additions in FY27 (34 so far), backed by a ~₹50,000 crore credit pipeline (₹18,000 crore sanctioned but undisbursed, ₹32,000 crore in hand), ECLGS 5.0 spillover of ₹5,000-6,000 crore, and FCNRB raising of USD 2.3-2.5 bn; no revenue growth % guided, and the ECL provision overhang (₹10,000-12,000 crore) weighs
